analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: Bonds' Redemption
key_insights: G4 10y yields sit 25-50bp below recent highs after equity market turbulence and energy price relief since end of October. GS expects yields to settle into a range and rate volatility to decline, provided risk asset volatility stays diminished and energy relief holds.
US: GS prefers longs in the belly of the curve, citing reduced front-end hike risk and a healthy labor market. It stays long 5s on the 2s5s30s fly and tightens the stop to -44bp.

US rates are driven mainly by energy and the AI trade post-midterms. Thursday's risk-off move produced bull steepening typical of a growth scare. The election should lift the fiscal spending baseline slightly but not change the debt trajectory.
The stronger-than-expected October US labor report keeps the Fed focused on inflation and makes it hard to remove more hike risk without favorable inflation news.
If risk assets stabilize, GS sees a 4.75-5.0% range on US 10y yields with room for rate volatility to moderate.

Breakevens underperformed their beta to oil this week, likely reflecting weakness in the AI trade. That left real yields historically cheap versus nominals on a beta-weighted basis, so GS adds a long 10y TIPS vs 0.75x short 10y nominals trade.

Treasury's November borrowing estimates are $618bn for 4Q26 and $800bn for 1Q27, slightly above GS projections, mainly because of a higher end-1Q27 cash balance. Coupon auction sizes are unchanged, and Treasury removed 'at least' from its guidance that sizes stay in place.

GS now expects coupon auction size increases from August 2027 (previously May), limited to the 2-10y sector. Risks skew toward modest cuts to 20y and 30y auction sizes. The upsized $6bn buyback envelope was affirmed.

Rates vol: under a baseline of cooling inflation and steady growth, GS sees the summer high-yield, low-vol environment as a playbook for next year and favors short-vol strategies. Because of tail risks it prefers overlaying short gamma with long vega. Further AI and growth concerns are the clearest route to higher vol, and 6m-to-1y low-strike receivers are the hedge, though they are expensive after the rally.

GS says relief rallies typically offer the best entry points for ATMF payers. A drop in implied vol, as has typically followed midterm elections, could be an opportunity for overlay hedges to a long duration bias.

Funding conditions are tighter, with higher repo rates and cheaper bills-OIS. Causes: elevated net bill supply, money fund AUM growth near zero since summer, and an elevated TGA. GS thinks the Fed is more likely to restart reserve management purchases and assumes $10bn of bill buying over the coming month.

Canada: a third consecutive weak payrolls report cut near-term BoC hike pricing, with the market shifting from December to January, where GS economists see the final hike. GS closes its CORH7Z7 flattener for a potential 11bp profit and would use hawkish repricing from US spillovers as a chance to re-engage in front-end longs.

Europe: about 40bp of ECB hike risk through end-2027 has come out since the late-September yield peak. Pricing is still more hawkish than GS's baseline of one more hike in December. GS sees limited room for further front-end decline and moves the stop on pay 1y1y EUR vs CHF to 2.91.
GS expects 5y to outperform on the EUR curve, since growth expectations are weaker, inflation forecasts are higher and rates vol has lagged the drop in commodity prices.

Belgium bonds have de-rated on deficit and political problems, with PM De Wever offering his resignation. The semi-core benefits more than peers from global relief. GS keeps its forecast of 10y OAT-Bund at 130bp by mid-2027, and says further compression needs credible deficit-reduction signals in France and Belgium.

UK: the BoE delivered its first hike with a vote split more hawkish than expected. GS economists expect one more hike in February. Gilts are a relative beneficiary of energy relief, with falling inflation compensation driving the rally, and GS keeps a medium-term steepening bias on the Gilt curve.

Scandis: the Riksbank raised to 2% and Norges Bank held at 4.5%, both as expected. GS expects two more Riksbank hikes to 2.5% next year and keeps its SEK flattening bias. Norges Bank's September hike is seen as the last, and GS favors steeper NOK curves relative to SEK.

Australia and NZ: the RBA hiked by split decision with a dovish-reading statement, and the market now prices cuts as early as March. GS recommends paying the February RBA OIS (entry 4.89, target 5.00, stop 4.85). In NZ, a weaker labor market delays hikes (next expected in February), supporting 2s10s steepeners.

Positioning data in the monitor: speculative duration-weighted net positions are negative across all listed futures contracts, including SFR -79.3, TY -58.5 and WN -61.4 ($mm/bp), while asset managers and others are net long in the USTs (TY +171.4).

GS projects higher Treasury issuance ahead: 2027 gross coupon sizes rise to 79 (2y), 68 (3y), 80 (5y) and 52 (7y), net bills of $984bn in CY2027 and total duration supply of $2,929bn (10y equivalents).

trade_ideas.risk: A renewed rise in front-end hike risk.

trade_ideas.rationale: Oil's October move and a possible hotter inflation print could reignite hike risk amid early signs of higher inflation expectations.

trade_ideas.description: Pay 1y1y EUR vs CHF, stop revised to 2.91 (opened 11-Sep-26 at 3.02, target 2.65)
trade_ideas.rationale: Limited room for further decline in very front-end pricing absent clearer energy supply progress.
Non-committal RBNZ tightening lets hike premium decay while term premium stays high.

trade_ideas.description: Close CORH7Z7 flattener for a potential 11bp profit
trade_ideas.rationale: Macklem's guidance on a possible neutral rate revision and recent price action worsen the risk-reward.

trade_ideas.description: Own 5s on the EUR curve for outperformance
trade_ideas.rationale: Weaker forward-looking growth, higher inflation forecasts and lagging rates vol favor the 5y.

trade_ideas.description: Steepening bias on the Gilt curve, steeper NOK curves relative to SEK, and an SEK curve-flattening bias
trade_ideas.rationale: Hike pricing in the UK is already extensive. NOK curves historically steepen after the final hike, while SEK front-end yields lead the adjustment at the start of a hiking cycle.
trade_ideas.risk: Renewed energy concerns could flatten the very front end of the UK curve.

risk_factors: A renewed energy price rise would reverse the relief in yields and bring UK and European hike risks forward.
A rebound in risk asset volatility or further AI and growth concerns could push rates vol higher.
Hotter-than-expected inflation could re-ignite hike risk, including for the RBA and the Fed.
Tighter funding conditions from bill supply, flat money fund AUM and an elevated TGA.
French and Belgian fiscal and political uncertainty could widen semi-core spreads.
US spillovers could drive hawkish repricing of the Canadian front end.
The energy relief may not extend, since further front-end ECB pricing declines require evidence of supply progress or clarity on winter weather.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots the 5-day change in 10y breakevens against the 5-day change in Brent, and breakevens underperformed their beta to the fall in oil prices this week.
Exhibit 2 shows real rates at the cheap end of their ex-Covid extreme range on a beta-weighted basis versus nominals.
Exhibit 3 shows implied vol typically embeds a vol premium going into midterm elections, which fades afterward.
Exhibit 4 shows the CAD front end typically reversed its initial rally after weaker employment data this year, in line with US yields.
Exhibit 5 shows rates volatility lagging the move lower in commodity prices.
Exhibit 6 shows the de-rating of Belgium bonds in recent months.
Exhibit 7 shows falling inflation compensation led the Gilt rally between 22 October and 5 November 2026.
Exhibit 8 shows NOK curves have historically steepened after the final hike of the cycle.
vol_and_positioning: Rates vol surged from cycle lows earlier in the year on AI disruption concerns and the US-Iran conflict, moderated through summer, then rebounded recently.
GS favors short-vol strategies under its benign baseline, overlaid with short gamma and long vega because of tail risks.
6m-to-1y low-strike receivers are the hedge against AI and growth-driven vol, but they are expensive after the rally and skew rotation toward receivers.
Implied USD vol typically embeds a premium going into midterm elections, which fades afterward. ATMF payers are best added during anticipatory relief rallies.
EUR rates vol has lagged the decline in commodity prices without a link to sovereign stress.
CFTC duration-weighted positioning: speculators net short across SFR, TU, FV, TY, TN, US and WN. Leveraged funds are also net short, and asset managers and others are net long in all but SFR.
GS positioning indicators: US OPI current score 0, US FPI current score -3, US DRI current score 1.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict is a key driver of energy prices and rates.
Improving geopolitical sentiment in the Middle East supports oil and gas risk premium reduction.
Belgian PM De Wever offered his resignation amid deficit and political uncertainty.
French fiscal and political uncertainty continues to weigh on semi-core sovereign spreads.
US midterm elections are expected to lift the fiscal spending baseline slightly without changing the debt trajectory.

tension_points.bull_case: Under a baseline of cooling inflation and steady growth, the summer environment of high yields and low volatility is a playbook for next year and supports short-vol strategies. Elevated starting yields and existing risk premia cap the scope for much higher vol on further sell-offs.
tension_points.bear_case: Pronounced tail risks warrant caution. Further AI and growth concerns are the clearest route to another leg higher in vol, and rates vol has rebounded recently after moderating through summer.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further AI and growth concerns would drive a higher leg in volatility, which GS hedges with 6m-to-1y low-strike receivers.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity turbulence and steep energy relief have anchored G4 10y yields 25-50bp below recent highs, and GS thinks yields can settle into a range with lower rate volatility.
tension_points.bear_case: The view hinges on diminished risk asset volatility and energy relief holding. Renewed energy concerns could bring UK and European hike risks forward.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy price relief failing to hold or risk asset volatility rising again.
